model_revision_cross_check.explanation: HPD-Parsing is not a v6 candidate; there is no prior pin in this repository to cross-check against. The only source is the official Hugging Face repository read today.

base_image_digest.resolution_detail: GET /v2/paddlepaddle/hpd-parsing-vllm/manifests/latest-nvidia-gpu-offline returned 401 with a Bearer challenge for realm https://ccr-auth.bj.baidubce.com/service/token, service ccr-2vdh3abv; the anonymous pull token from that realm made the same GET return 200 with this Docker-Content-Digest. Same value as build/build_plan.json models.hpd_parsing.base_image.digest (lane F).

base_image_alternatives.note: The offline image (~24.5 GB) bakes the weights; the online image (~20.2 GB) downloads them on first use. Only moving `latest-*` tags are published, which is why a build-time digest is mandatory.

license_notes: Apache-2.0 on the weights repository. The customized vLLM wheel and the official container image are separate artifacts under their own terms, and an OSS licence is not patent freedom to operate.

quoted_vendor_claims.note: Quoted from the official tutorial, never reproduced by this campaign.

to_verify_in_canary: base_image_digest is resolved: the earlier 401 was an unauthenticated first hop, not a refusal - the registry advertises a Bearer realm and issues an anonymous pull token. runtime.json.base_image now carries name:tag@sha256:<digest>. The image config declares its own ENTRYPOINT (/bin/bash /home/hpd/entrypoint.sh), so bootstrap mode must override it through RunPod REST v1 dockerEntrypoint (ARENA_CONTRACT D2); confirm at canary time that the override actually took effect.
model_revision_cross_check.recorded_revision and .agrees are null because HPD-Parsing has no prior pin in benchmark/v6/candidate-registry.yaml to compare against.

max_concurrency_per_worker is 8 as a starting point only: the docs say throughput comes from concurrent requests and show a 16-thread client pool, but publish no per-GPU number. The canary decides the value, and it must be lowered on any TENSOR_SHAPE or OUTPUT_TRUNCATED cluster.

The offline image bakes weights; confirm at canary time that the baked revision equals model_revision, and record the P-MTP directory digest too. If the image's revision differs, this build's explicit `hf download --revision` is already correct and the discrepancy is the finding.

FLASHINFER and CUDA >= 12.8 are hard requirements of the official build; confirm the provisioned GPU and driver satisfy them, and that FLASHINFER is actually the selected attention backend rather than a silent substitute.
gpu_pool_priority holds RunPod gpuTypeId strings for the officially verified 80 GB-class hardware; confirm each against the provider catalog snapshot.
Record the finish_reason == 'length' rate at max_tokens 8000. A high rate means pages are being truncated, which is a quality finding and not a runtime one.

checkpoint.declared_transformers_version: absent - the checkpoint's config.json carries no transformers_version field

framework_floor_audit.required: the model card requires a customized vLLM build, distributed as the prebuilt wheel vllm-0.17.1+hpdparsing-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_31_x86_64.whl, and CUDA 12.8+. Upstream vllm v0.17.1's registry.py carries "InternVLChatModel": ("internvl", "InternVLChatModel").
framework_floor_audit.image_ships: the official offline image hpd-parsing-vllm:latest-nvidia-gpu-offline is documented to carry that customized build; its exact version string is unknown from evidence until the pod reports it, which bootstrap.sh already records as vllm_version
framework_floor_audit.action: no pin added - the prebuilt wheel fallback bootstrap.sh already carries is the vendor's only other documented path. What changed: the preflight now FAILS CLOSED when the installed vLLM's local version does not carry '+hpdparsing' (it was previously only recorded into the receipt), and it asks the registry for InternVLChatModel before the server starts.

cuda_floor.source: max(base image CUDA runtime, vendor documented floor)
cuda_floor.vendor_documented_floor: 12.8, from the model card requirement already recorded in this file under environment_requirements.cuda (">=12.8") and quoted_vendor_claims. Both halves agree, so the max is 12.8.
cuda_floor.rationale: min_cuda_version is the lowest CUDA version a RunPod host may report for this runtime to start. It is sent as the create payload's allowedCudaVersions -- every version RunPod lists at or above it -- because pod 3xag0y00rgoj4n ran this campaign's CUDA 12.9 image on a host reporting cudaVersion 12.8 and died in torch._C._cuda_init with CUDA error 804 after the pod was already billing. Read anonymously from the pinned image's own OCI config blob at the digest runtime.json pins; nothing is inferred from the image name.
